headline: Council on Aging

meeting.summary: The Council on Aging had ethics training and heard the office won $390,000 for a program helping older adults leaving the hospital.
meeting.recap: The Council on Aging met at 12:30 p.m. on September 8, 2026.[[0:00:39]] A Board of Ethics staff member gave a training on the code of ethics.[[0:08:12]] Members agreed that anyone who thinks they may have a conflict should email the ethics office.[[0:31:38]] A Lānaʻi member said a storm badly damaged the harbor that receives gasoline and food.[[0:42:49]] A Hāna member reported landslides and fallen trees on Hāna Highway.[[0:44:14]] The program will link older adults leaving the hospital with a community health worker for 90 days.[[0:50:23]] The rural health funds must be encumbered, or committed, by September 30th.[[1:01:38]] A program bringing locally grown fruits and vegetables to kūpuna (elders) started last week.[[1:06:18]] The office is helping an older adult cited for an unpermitted addition to her home.[[1:08:19]] The office helped check on people on the Big Island after a hurricane.[[1:18:18]] State aging executives are likely to meet in the next couple of days on emergency preparedness.[[1:19:22]]
decided: Members agreed that anyone who feels they may have a conflict should email the ethics office.
meeting.next: The council secretary was asked to put the ethics office email contact in the minutes. The ethics office asks members to call three days before a meeting if a question involves a vote or deliberation. In the next couple of weeks, the office will gather and analyze survey data and then work on objectives for the four-year plan. It was suggested that a Maui emergency group be invited to give an emergency preparedness presentation.

moments.q: "The harbor where we receive our gasoline and our food supplies is like destroyed."
"It's as if I'm building the ship as it's sailing."
